messages:
emily: flagging something odd from the recent reranker bring-up on long documents. after PTQ int8 conversion we see a small overall NDCG dip but a disproportionate number of rank flips for long-doc queries (several T3 customers reported degraded relevance). anyone digging into int8s effect specifically for long context?

rajan: we saw int8 amplify some peaked logits in a separate ranking probe. could be out-of-range activations causing different softmax dynamics for long context where attention patterns change. do you have a repro slice?

emily: yes  dataset slice: longdoc-queries-v3 (mean doc tokens ~3600, truncated to 4k for encoder). summary: FP16 NDCG@10=0.797, PTQ-INT8=0.776 (-2.6%). MRR@1 almost flat. but per-query analysis shows ~5% of queries have top-1 swapped to unrelated candidate. attached short log below.

lucas: can you paste the small diagnostics? even short snippets help.

emily: here: 
```
probe: longdoc-queries-v3, sample=2k, seed=13
variant fp16: ndcg10=0.797, mrr1=0.502
variant ptq-int8: ndcg10=0.776, mrr1=0.499
rank_flip_count=102 (of 2000)
avg_logit_kl(fp16||int8)=0.085
top1_unrelated_fraction=0.032
cohort_docs>3k_tokens: ndcg_drop=4.1%
```

nina: interesting that MRR is flat but NDCG drops - suggests tail of ranking worsened or batchwise rescoring differences. rank_flip_count 102 is worrying. i'd look at per-layer activation outliers and the final layer norm stats between precisions. also compare softmax temperature sensitivity.

rajan: agreed. propose these quick diagnostics: 1) collect activation percentiles (min/median/99.9) for a small subset, 2) compute per-candidate logit delta distribution fp16->int8, 3) run score calibration post-hoc (learn scalar temp or bias) and measure ndcg recovery.

emily: i tried a quick calibration: fit a scalar temperature on a holdout and re-evaluate. softmax temp=0.92 recovers ~0.6% of NDCG but not full. attaching script snippet used.

lucas: we should also test QAT (fast fine-tune with fake quant) vs PTQ to see if learned offset helps. QAT sometimes fixes rank ordering by allowing the network to adjust. can we carve a tiny QAT job on a small subset?

emily: queued a 2-epoch QAT job with 8k examples (longdoc subset) using our small lr schedule. expected runtime ~4h on a single gpu.

nina: another axis: candidate normalization. for long docs candidate representations might be noisier; try l2-normalize logits or limit dynamic range with clip. also compute cosine similarity of embeddings vs logit ordering to see if reranker deviates more under int8.

rajan: add to ablation grid: precision (fp16/ptq-int8/qat-int8), calibration (none/temp/affine), candidate-clipping (none/clip0.1/clip0.5), metric slicing (top1 flips, ndcg tail deciles). run 3 seeds for each small job. keep sample=1k per run to iterate.

emily: i'll push gauntlet jobs: `longdoc_precision_ablation.{prec}.{calib}.{clip}.{seed}` and tag results to eval dashboard.

eval-bot: eval run 1765441001 started  config: longdoc_precision_ablation.ptq-int8.none.none.seed13 sample=1000 metrics=[NDCG@10,MRR@1,rank_flip_count]

lucas: for immediate mitigations in prod: 1) enable post-score calibration layer (cheap), 2) fall back to FP16 on queries with doc_tokens>2k (more expensive), or 3) use ensemble of fp16+int8 scoring for at-risk cohorts. pros/cons?

emily: i prefer 1 for short-term (deployable as a model-agnostic scaler) and 3 for safety if critical customers complain. fallback (2) is heavy but worth if QAT doesn't resolve.

nina: please add detailed per-query examples for the top1 flips to the ticket (include doc id, query text, fp16 top1, int8 top1, logits). helps root cause.

emily: will attach 20 example flips and the activation percentile dumps when QAT finishes. thanks all. :thumbsup:
